items.title: 68189_Al Hall oral history interview
items.q: And we gave him hell. Don't speak to him anymore.

ctx.x: Right. Right. Barney Joseph con thinks he's an impresario, but he didn't do it himself. John Hammond did it for him. He would take the credit now, but when I was hired that isn't the way I saw it in 1940.

I can remember one night Albert Ammons, the (inaudible) Boogie-woogie pianist (inaudible) came in. Barney was standing at the door, and Albert spoke to him. Barney didn't answer him, and he came back to the dressing room crying (inaudible). And we gave him hell. Don't speak to him anymore.
